validity.recommendation: none for existence/classification/ownership/diameter/capacity/status — see the four concern entries below for value-level and location-direction issues that need a human call
validity.researcher_notes: Existence confirmed independently of GEM/gem.wiki and of the sheet's own three cited leads (only one of which, the niobium.tech PDF of Jahde/Al-Sharif/Starke 2007 'Independence Trail Gas Trunkline and Challenges of Ultra Deepwater and Harsh Environment Pipelines' (Enterprise Field Services LLC engineers, TMS conference proceedings), verifies live and names the pipeline; the A Barrel Full citation is banned and the OnePetro OTC-19056-MS abstract page 403s behind a Cloudflare challenge from every client tried). Five additional independent origins found via open-web search all describe the same real, in-service pipeline: Oil & Gas Journal (three separate articles: a Jan-2006 expansion notice, a Nov-27-2006 special report, and a 2008 leak/resumption notice), a joint Anadarko/Enterprise/Devon/Eni/Hydro BusinessWire press release on first production (archived; Anadarko's investor-relations subdomain no longer resolves live), offshore-technology.com's Independence Hub project page (archived), Enterprise Products' own official company-history page, and Allseas' own company-history page (the pipelay contractor, naming the 'Independence Trail project' by its common short name in a list of Solitaire's technical milestones). This is a real, correctly-classified interstate-equivalent OCS gas trunk line (Fuel=Gas correct; not a gathering/process line — it exists specifically to move already-processed sales gas from the Independence Hub central processing platform to a downstream pipeline interconnect, the textbook definition of a transmission/export trunk), and it does not duplicate any other PID in the 50-row roster (no other Independence-, West Delta-, or Mississippi Canyon-named row exists in the roster; P0217 'Mississippi Canyon Gas Pipeline' is a physically distinct, separately-FERC/BOEM-tracked system per its own 44.5-mile length and different block numbers). Diameter=24in confirmed at high tier — every one of the seven documents opened (niobium.tech, OGJ x3, Anadarko PR, offshore-technology.com, Enterprise history) states 24 inches, no disagreement. Capacity=1000.00 MMcf/d confirmed at high tier and independently: niobium.tech states 'the requirements of 1.0 Billion Cubic Feet (BCF) per day gas throughput'; the Anadarko/BusinessWire release states 'the capacity to transport up to 1 Bcf/d'; OGJ's Nov-2006 special report states 'a capacity of 1 bcfd' — Enterprise (pipeline owner) and Anadarko (Hub operator, a different company) are two independent origins agreeing exactly, with OGJ trade press as a third. Fuel=Gas is trivially correct (every source describes a natural-gas trunk line). Status=operating confirmed: first gas flowed July 19, 2007 (Anadarko/BusinessWire release, dateline Jul 20 2007), and although OGJ reported the line was shut in after 'a leak that occurred Apr. 8' 2008 near a flex-joint in ~85 ft of water, repairs were completed and reduced-then-full volumes resumed by early-to-mid June 2008 (OGJ, 'Independence Trail pipeline resumes operations') — a repaired outage, not a status change, consistent with the BOEM-status rule for GoM lines (decommissioned/abandoned is a status finding; a repaired leak on an otherwise-live line is not). Owner1= Enterprise Products Partners 100% confirmed at high tier: Anadarko/BusinessWire ('100 percent owned and operated by Enterprise'), OGJ special report ('a wholly owned affiliate of Enterprise Products Partners LP'), and Enterprise's own company-history page all agree — two of these are origins independent of Enterprise itself (Anadarko, OGJ). Note in passing (not a tracker data issue): gem.wiki's own page is still tagged with the MediaWiki category 'Proposed pipelines in the United States' despite the article text and the sheet's Status=operating both being correct — a stale wiki-side category, not something that affects this row's GEM database values. Opened to exhaustion: niobium.tech PDF (full text), all three OGJ articles (full paragraph-level extraction), the archived Anadarko/BusinessWire release (full text), the archived offshore-technology.com project page, Enterprise's own history page, and Allseas' history page — 7 of the row's independently-found documents read in full, plus the sheet's own 3 harvested wiki citations (1 banned, 1 blocked/unverifiable, 1 used as the row's anchor primary source).

validity.recommendation: verify whether StartLocation/EndLocation should be swapped (Mississippi Canyon Block 920 as Start, West Delta Block 68 as End) to match actual gas-flow direction and this roster's own Start=upstream-field/End=downstream-delivery convention; separately, correct FuelSource off 'West Delta Block 68' to the actual upstream source (Independence Hub / Mississippi Canyon Block 920 fields)
validity.researcher_notes: Four independent sources describing the pipeline's function all agree on ONE gas-flow direction: Mississippi Canyon Block 920 (the Independence Hub central processing platform, the upstream source) toward West Delta Block 68 (a shallow-water manifold platform where the gas interconnects with — and is delivered into — Tennessee Gas Pipeline for onward transport to onshore markets). Anadarko/BusinessWire: 'connects the Hub platform to onshore markets via an interconnect with the Tennessee Gas Pipeline at Enterprise's West Delta block 68 shallow-water manifold platform.' OGJ (Jan 2006): pipeline 'will transport the gas to the Tennessee Gas Pipeline system in West Delta Block 68.' OGJ (Nov 2006 special report): 'connects the Independence Hub [platform] to an interconnect with Tennessee Gas Pipeline in West Delta Block 68.' Allseas (contractor, own history page): 'the pipeline transports gas from the Independence Hub Facility in Mississippi Canyon 920 to the West Delta 68 platform.' The sheet's current Location [ref] unit has StartLocation='West Delta Block 68' and EndLocation='Mississippi Canyon Block 920' — i.e. the REVERSE of the direction every independent source describes. The one source that reads consistently with the sheet's current direction is the sheet's own cited primary lead, niobium.tech (Jahde et al. 2007, written by the pipeline's own design engineers): 'ITP initiates from West Delta Block 68... and terminates at Mississippi Canyon Block 920' — but read in context this sentence is in the 'Pipeline Route Selection' section describing how the pipe-LAY vessel worked (shallow water to deep water), not the direction gas flows once in service; Allseas' own account of the SAME lay operation (Solitaire delivering the project in 2006) states the finished pipeline moves gas the opposite way. This roster's other offshore-to-onshore rows (P0223 Nautilus: 'Ship Shoal Block 207, Green Canyon Corridor -> Louisiana'; P0217 Mississippi Canyon Gas Pipeline: 'Mississippi Canyon -> Louisiana') consistently put the upstream field as Start and the downstream delivery point as End, so a swap here would also align this row with the roster's own convention. This is not a phantom-pipeline or duplicate concern — the place names in the Location cell are both correct and independently verified, it is only the Start/End assignment (and the copy of that assignment into FuelSource) that is doubtful. FuelSource is separately wrong on the same logic: the GEM schema gotcha for gas-sheet FuelSource is 'the upstream gas source feeding the line — a field, plant, or facility,' not a downstream delivery point, so 'West Delta Block 68' (the TGP interconnect/exit point) is very likely backwards for this column too; the correct value is the Independence Hub platform / the Atwater Valley-DeSoto Canyon-Lloyd Ridge-Mississippi Canyon field complex it gathers (OGJ special report names the ten anchor fields feeding the Hub). Left as a validity flag rather than an auto-fix per the 'never auto-apply a reference value' rule and because the StartState/Province='Gulf of Mexico' / EndState/Province='Gulf of Mexico' pair is genuinely defensible as written — this pipeline is subsea/offshore end-to-end between two OCS platforms and never itself makes onshore landfall in any state (delivery to shore happens downstream, inside Tennessee Gas Pipeline), so no state-name correction is proposed for either State/Province cell; this differs from the scope note's other flagged rows (Garden Banks, etc.) where a real state IS available.

validity.recommendation: flag LengthKnown=138.00 mi for review — the best-corroborated independent figure is 134 mi, not 138
validity.researcher_notes: Three distinct length figures circulate for this one pipeline, not two: (1) 140 miles / 225 km — Enterprise Products' own official company-history page ('a 24-inch, 140-mile pipeline at an estimated cost of $280 million') and offshore-technology.com's project page ('140 miles (225km) of 24in-diameter pipeline... total cost of the pipeline was estimated at $280m') both give this figure, and both attach it to the same $280m cost estimate — this is the ORIGINAL, pre-construction 2004 planning estimate, not an as-built number (Enterprise's history page places this sentence under the original 2004 Atwater Valley Producers Group agreement, before construction). (2) 134 miles — Oil & Gas Journal, in three separate articles, and the joint Anadarko/Enterprise/Devon/Eni/Hydro BusinessWire release on first production, state 'a new 134-mile, 24-in. pipeline' / 'the pipeline is approximately 134 miles long' / '134 miles on the seafloor' — OGJ's Nov-27-2006 special report gives this figure with the pipeline already S-laid (Allseas Solitaire completed the lay in August 2006), i.e. this is a near-as-built figure from two independent origins (OGJ the trade press, and Anadarko the Hub operator — a company distinct from Enterprise). (3) 138 miles — the sheet's current value, matching only the niobium.tech Jahde et al. 2007 conference paper written by the pipeline's own Enterprise design engineers, published after the line entered service. None of the three post-construction/as-built sources (OGJ x2 distinct events, Anadarko) agree with the sheet's 138; the only match is the single Enterprise engineering paper, which is a credible, specific, technical source but is one origin. Weight of independent evidence favors 134 mi over 138, but given a real engineering paper states 138 explicitly (not a rounding artifact — it is used consistently throughout that paper's methodology, e.g. in the deepwater length used for the world-record claim), this is presented as a flagged discrepancy for Baird to weigh rather than a value I'm confident enough to recommend silently overwriting. No fix applied; LengthKnown is left as-is on the sheet pending review.

validity.recommendation: verify ProposalYear — an independent trade-press source dates the proposal to 2003, not 2004
validity.researcher_notes: The sheet's ProposalYear=2004 has no ref and, on the direct evidence found, is arguably one year off. OGJ's Nov-27-2006 special report states explicitly: 'The companies proposed to build the platform and pipeline in 2003, with procurement starting in 2004 along with the agreements for the ownership infrastructure, processing, and transportation.' The public ANNOUNCEMENT of the specific agreements (the one most sources anchor to) was Nov. 10, 2004 (OGJ Online dateline, repeated across several 2004-2006 OGJ articles), which is likely why 2004 ended up in the sheet — but per this special report the underlying proposal/decision to build predates that by roughly a year. I did not find a second, independent source that states a specific proposal year (most sources just cite the Nov. 2004 announcement date without characterizing it as 'the proposal year' one way or the other), so this is presented as a single well-sourced discrepancy for review rather than a confident fill/correction — searched Enterprise's own company-history page and the Anadarko/BusinessWire release for a corroborating or conflicting proposal year and found neither; both just describe the Nov-2004 agreements without dating 'the proposal' itself.

summary: P0204 Independence Trail: real, correctly-classified, independently-confirmed OCS gas trunk (Enterprise-owned/operated, Anadarko-fed Independence Hub); 5 fields sourced (ConstructionYear=2006, StartMonth1=July, Pressure=3640psi, SegmentCost=$280m est., Operator=Enterprise) but 4 concerns flagged for review — Length (138 vs. the better-corroborated 134mi), ProposalYear (2004 vs. a source dating it 2003), and a likely Start/End + FuelSource direction reversal (WD68/MC920 backwards vs. actual gas flow and the roster's own convention).
